newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: COUNTRY ROAD SAYS NO COMMENT ON ARI LETTER.
newsitem.headline: COUNTRY ROAD SAYS NO COMMENT ON ARI LETTER.

text.p: Country Road Ltd on Wednesday said it would not comment on a letter sent to the company on Tuesday which complained the value of the fashion retailer's brand was diminishing.

The letter from J.T. Campbell & Co Pty Ltd, advisers to Australian Retail Investments Pty Ltd (ARI) which own about nine percent of Country Road Ltd, said ARI believed the Country Road brand had been eroded and was at risk of further damage.
"The company has decided it will not respond to ARI through the media," a Country Road spokesman told Reuters.
Tuesday's letter follows a profit downgrade from the retailer last week which indicated the group's full year earnings could be lower than its half profit after abnormals of A$1.09 million.
Late on Tuesday, Country Road's major shareholder, South African clothing retailer Wooltru Ltd, said it had increased its holding in Country Road to 19.74 percent from 14.86 percent.
The spokesman said Country Road was happy with Wooltru's decision to raise its stake.

Under Australian share ownership rules, Wooltru cannot lift its stake above 19.9 percent without making an offer to all shareholders. But it can use creep provisions to buy three percent of the company's stock every six months.
Wooltru director Syd Muller is already a member of the Country Road board.
At 12.00 p.m (0200 GMT), Country Road shares were two cents weaker at A$1.52.
